captured_note: Ported from the capture's self-contained methods/26_simmim, specifically its Swin-B step 1 (models/simmim_swinb.py, data/simmim_dataset.py, train_pretrain_swinb.py, evaluate_linear.py). These are the lab's own implementation of Xie et al. (2022) SimMIM, following microsoft/SimMIM. The pretrain code builds timm's SwinTransformer from scratch (measured: the `transformers` package appears only in a docstring note about HuggingFace pretrained weights and is never imported), so this ports self-contained and needs only timm. The port keeps the capture directory numbering (26) per the 2026-08-09 keep-capture-numbering decision (see docs/PORTING_ROADMAP.md).

paper.title: SimMIM: A Simple Framework for Masked Image Modeling
paper.authors: Xie, Zhang, Cao, Lin, Bao, Yao, Dai, Hu

scope: The Swin-B step 1 is ported: images are patch-embedded by a Swin encoder; a random block of patch tokens (mask units of 32x32 pixels = 8x8 Swin patches, 60% masked) is replaced by a learned mask token; the full token grid is encoded by Swin; a 1x1 conv + PixelShuffle decoder reconstructs pixels; an L1 loss is taken only on the masked pixels. AdamW under a per-iteration schedule (linear warmup then a multistep decay), the base LR optionally scaled by the global batch size; gradient-norm clipping. The capture's unified step 2 (ViT-B/16) is also ported additively (recipe: unified); see rewritten_during_the_port.
encoder: encoder.pt is the bare Swin encoder (encoder.*, the prefix stripped so it loads straight into a plain timm SwinTransformer): the patch embed, the Swin stages and the final norm, producing the mean-pooled feature (encoder_dim; 1024 for Swin-B). The learned mask token (mask_token) and the reconstruction decoder (decoder.*) are training machinery and are excluded -- the standard SSL convention of probing the encoder.
linear_eval: Reads the trained encoder.pt and probes the Swin encoder's mean-pooled forward_features (encoder_dim), a genuine learned representation, so the number is comparable. Images use the deterministic val pipeline (resize + centre crop, ImageNet normalisation -- the same normalisation SimMIM trains with). The capture's own SimMIM eval standardises the cached features (zero mean / unit std) then fits a linear head; this port follows the lab's shared ARSSL probe (mean-centre + L2-normalise features, single linear layer, SGD momentum + cosine, top1/top5) rather than the capture's own head, so the number is comparable across the ported methods.
rewritten_during_the_port: only the Swin-B step 1 is ported; the capture's step 2 (ViT) is excluded, as in every port

timm supplies the SwinTransformer (built from scratch, no pretrained download, so the run stays hermetic); the transformers package listed in the capture's requirements.txt is docstring-only and never imported (measured), so it is not a dependency of this port
build_swin_encoder is a single construction path shared by the SimMIM model and the linear-eval loader, so the encoder is built one way
img_size and the Swin dims are threaded so a small hermetic CPU smoke runs a tiny 2-stage Swin at a lower resolution
the mask generator, the mask-token replacement, the Conv+PixelShuffle decoder and the masked-pixel L1 loss are kept faithfully (all torch); step 1 uses patch-grid masks
the device is resolved (resolve_device) instead of assumed CUDA (the capture called .cuda())
main() split into build_parser()/run(args, config) returning the pretext loss and epoch count
the run is seeded through make_deterministic (python, numpy, torch); the DataLoader gets a seeded generator

the training loop drops the upstream DistributedDataParallel, the AMP autocast/GradScaler and TensorBoard/tqdm so the same step runs on a CPU or a GPU unchanged, single-process fp32; the per-iteration warmup + multistep LR schedule and the global-batch LR scaling are kept

the capture's unified step 2 (ViT-B/16) is added additively, selected by a recipe: unified key in train (absent == the native Swin-B step-1 path, unchanged). Unlike the other ViT Step-2 ports, SimMIM's native backbone is a Swin, so the unified Step 2 is a different backbone: models/simmim_vit.py is ported (a timm ViT-B/16 with pixel-space masking, a learned per-channel mask token, a Linear(embed_dim -> 3*p*p) head and an L1 loss on masked patches). build_vit_encoder threads the ViT dims through timm.create_model (the capture used the fixed vit_base_patch16_224 name) so a small hermetic CPU smoke can run a tiny ViT; it is the single construction path shared by the SimMIM wrapper and the adapter's load_encoder.

train_pretrain_vit_simmim.py is a single-process port of the capture's train_step2_vit.py: the lr is used directly (the capture baked lr=1.5e-4*1024/256=6e-4 into the config), AdamW with the config betas, a linear warmup then cosine decay to min_lr, gradient-norm clipping, and milestone checkpoints (checkpoint_epoch_{N}.pth at save_at_epochs). It reuses resolve_device/make_deterministic from the native trainer; DDP, AMP and TensorBoard are dropped. The pixel-resolution mask comes from get_simmim_dataloader(return_pixel_mask=True), one mask unit = one ViT patch.

this is the only Step-2 port non-additive to the eval: the native probe mean-pools the Swin tokens, but the ViT's representation is its CLS token (the capture's own choice), so evaluate_linear_simmim.py gains a pool argument (cls for the ViT, mean for the Swin), fixed from the recipe by the adapter (adapter.eval_pool). The adapter also gained a recipe: unified branch (disjoint key sets), a ViT load_encoder branch, and milestone encoder_epoch{N}.pt extraction; configs/pretrain_vit.yaml and configs/linear_eval_vit.yaml are added.
